**Finding submitted: MISSING (insurance clause absent).**

- **What I checked:** The whole agreement is a single body of 75 paragraphs; a search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the General Provisions (§14, p0064–p0073) cover only governing law, publicity, independent contractor, fees, notices, severability/survival, force majeure, assignment and third-party beneficiaries.
- **Why it matters:** Kubient is a hosting/services vendor — it hosts the Auction Platform (p0002, p0005) and warrants in p0035 that it collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information (data). Under the playbook that combination requires E&O and cyber cover; no insurance at all for a vendor processing personal data is the walk-away position.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** New §14(j) inserted after p0073 requiring CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, professional (E&O) USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, running through the Term plus one year, with certificates on request. I tailored the cyber trigger to this deal's language ("collection, maintenance, management and storage of Customer's and its visitors' data and Confidential Information") because "Customer Data" is not a defined term here.
- **Negotiation posture:** Comment flags the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if Kubient resists the preferred limits. The clause binds only the counterparty, so it adds no obligation on AP.
